Reversible

/rih-VER-suh-buhl/ - the stress falls on VER · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Reversible means capable of being undone or returned to a previous state.

Conservators insist on reversible treatments, so tomorrow's restorers can lift today's varnish without a trace.

Worked Example

The wedding planner drafts every seating plan in pencil. Couples merge tables, feuds erupt, a cousin says yes at the last hour — and each new crisis costs one pass of the eraser. Ink would make every change a fresh sheet of paper; pencil keeps the whole plan reversible until the morning of.

Reversible is exact because it promises a road back to the previous state — not that the change is small, and not that it will end on its own. A banner hung for one weekend is temporary; a reversible decision comes down whenever you choose. The power to un-choose is the whole idea.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

undoable: able to be undone — the plain workhorse twin

restorable: able to be brought back to an earlier state

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

indelible: impossible to erase — inks, stains, impressions

one-way: admitting no return trip — doors, valves, and choices

Where it sits · how fully the original state returns — mendable → correctable → reversible

mendable vs. reversible: Mendable means the damage can be patched, though seams and scars may stay; reversible promises the cleaner miracle — back to exactly how it was.

correctable vs. reversible: A correctable error can be set right going forward; reversible reaches further back, unwinding the change as though it had never happened.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back

Root — vers

Root — vers: to turn

Suffix — -ible

Suffix — -ible: able to be

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (back) + vers (to turn, from Latin vertere) + -ible (able to be) = able to be turned back. The same gears as this unit's irreversible, minus the lock: what turned once can turn again. English keeps the pair as a matched set — one word the swinging door, the other the door welded shut.

Use the root in a new word: version

Use the root in a new word: version: The museum displays an early version of the map beside the final one.

Word Choice

neutral / precise

Reversible certifies an exit: the change can be unmade and the previous state restored. Don't mistake it for temporary, which ends on its own schedule — a reversible policy may last forever, so long as the road back stays open. Its unit-mates irreversible and irrevocable name the two ways the road closes: a process with no way back, a promise with no calling back.
